sections.heading: Installation
sections.text:
ttsready 0.2 requires Python 3.10 or newer. Install it with pip:

python -m pip install ttsready




The library’s runtime dependencies are spokenform>=0.4.5,<0.5 and phrasplit>=0.3.9,<1. The package does not install format parsers, file readers, a CLI framework, or an audio renderer.

Install the optional lexical extra when using integrations that need the lexhint lexical-evidence package:

python -m pip install 'ttsready[lexical]'




For development, install the development tools and tests:

python -m pip install 'ttsready[dev]'




Continue with the quickstart or the full Python API reference.

sections.heading: Lexical review
sections.text: review_lexicon() identifies caller-owned words that may deserve pronunciation or vocabulary review. It is an analysis helper only: it does not modify text, fetch a lexicon, or require an evidence provider. The operation and result types are exported from the root ttsready package.
sections.lower: review_lexicon() identifies caller-owned words that may deserve pronunciation or vocabulary review. it is an analysis helper only: it does not modify text, fetch a lexicon, or require an evidence provider. the operation and result types are exported from the root ttsready package.

sections.heading: Inputs
sections.text:
review_lexicon(units: Iterable[TextUnit] | PreparationResult, *, provider=None, max_frequency_rank=10_000, min_count=1, max_items=None, unknown_only=False, include_all_tokens=False) -> LexicalReviewResult accepts an iterable of caller-owned TextUnit values or a PreparationResult. The evidence provider is optional.

from ttsready import TextUnit, review_lexicon

units = (TextUnit("chapter-1", "We met Siobhan.", "en"),)
review = review_lexicon(
    units,
    max_frequency_rank=10_000,
    min_count=1,
    include_all_tokens=True,
)

sections.heading: Results
Candidate reasons
Filtering behavior
sections.text:
URL, email, and domain-like spans are excluded from lexical review.


Tokens overlapping a TextUnit.protected_spans span are excluded.


Numeric-only material is not treated as a lexical word.


unknown_only=True retains only terms for which a provider explicitly returns known is False. Without that evidence, known is None and no term can satisfy this filter.


include_all_tokens=True includes otherwise eligible tokens even when no review reason applies. By default, only terms with at least one reason are returned.



Filtering never removes or changes text; it only controls which findings are returned.

sections.heading: Optional Lexhint provider
sections.text:
The lexhint integration is optional. Construct and manage the provider explicitly; TTSReady does not download datasets or select a lexicon on the caller’s behalf.

from lexhint import Lexicon
from ttsready import TextUnit, review_lexicon

lexicon = Lexicon("en", variant="runtime")
review = review_lexicon(
    (TextUnit("chapter-1", "We met Siobhan.", "en"),),
    provider=lexicon,
)

for finding in review.findings:
    print(finding.surface, finding.reasons, finding.known, finding.frequency_rank)




Install the optional extra with python -m pip install 'ttsready[lexical]' when using Lexhint. See installation and the Python API inventory.

entries.title: ttsready Migration from 0.1.x
entries.snippet: Version 0.2 is a breaking release that narrows ttsready to a source-neutral preparation API. It does not preserve 0.1 application behavior b …

sections.heading: Migration from 0.1.x
sections.text: Version 0.2 is a breaking release that narrows ttsready to a source-neutral preparation API. It does not preserve 0.1 application behavior behind compatibility wrappers.
sections.lower: version 0.2 is a breaking release that narrows ttsready to a source-neutral preparation api. it does not preserve 0.1 application behavior behind compatibility wrappers.

sections.heading: Removed ownership
sections.text:
The following 0.1 areas are no longer part of ttsready:


SSMD and document/book parsing, source-specific models, file readers, and writers.


CLI commands, reporting workflows, caches, sidecars, planning, selection, and freeze/materialization.


Speaker/JEV scanning, registries, and speaker annotation workflows.


File-based locks, exports, and document-owned reproducibility operations.



Callers now own source parsing and I/O, output formats, workflow state, and persistence. The library accepts only caller-owned text data and returns in-memory values.

cli commands, reporting workflows, caches, sidecars, planning, selection, and freeze/materialization.


speaker/jev scanning, registries, and speaker annotation workflows.


file-based locks, exports, and document-owned reproducibility operations.



callers now own source parsing and i/o, output formats, workflow state, and persistence. the library accepts only caller-owned text data and returns in-memory values.

sections.heading: Replace the 0.1 preparation flow
sections.text:
A file- or document-oriented call such as load(...), load_ssmd(...), prepare_tts_plan(...), or a CLI command must be moved to the caller’s adapter. Pass the text and language directly to the library:

from ttsready import TextUnit, prepare_text, prepare_units

# One text unit:
prepared = prepare_text(source_text, language="en-US", unit_id="chapter-1")
print(prepared.spoken_text)

# Or an ordered set with per-unit language:
result = prepare_units(
    (
        TextUnit("chapter-1", source_text, "en-US", role="body"),
        TextUnit("caption-1", caption_text, "fr-FR", role="caption"),
    )
)




prepare_text() returns a PreparedUnit; prepare_units() returns a PreparationResult. Both expose exact source-relative changes, issues, and contexts. apply_changes() verifies and applies a change…

sections.heading: Policy and state
sections.text: Replace document annotations with caller-owned SpeechOverride values. Use global, unit, or occurrence scopes as appropriate; see overrides. Use check_units() and the issues attached to preparation results for residual QA. Use pure fingerprints and JSON serialization when building caller-owned records; ttsready no longer maintains caches, lock files, or persistent review state.

entries.title: ttsready Speech overrides
entries.snippet: A SpeechOverride maps a source surface to caller-chosen spoken text. It can match literal substrings or whole words, case-sensitively or cas …

sections.heading: Speech overrides
sections.text: A SpeechOverride maps a source surface to caller-chosen spoken text. It can match literal substrings or whole words, case-sensitively or case-insensitively, and can be scoped to all units, one unit, or one exact occurrence.
sections.lower: a speechoverride maps a source surface to caller-chosen spoken text. it can match literal substrings or whole words, case-sensitively or case-insensitively, and can be scoped to all units, one unit, or one exact occurrence.

sections.heading: Global and unit-scoped overrides
sections.text:
from ttsready import OverrideScope, SpeechOverride, TextUnit, prepare_units

unit = TextUnit("chapter-1", "ACME ships 2 kg parcels.", "en-US")
company = SpeechOverride("ACME", "A C M E")  # all units
weight = SpeechOverride(
    "kg",
    "kilograms",
    scope=OverrideScope("unit", "chapter-1"),
)
result = prepare_units((unit,), overrides=(company, weight))




The default match mode is word. Use match="literal" to match a substring inside a larger token. The default is case-sensitive; set case_sensitive=False for case-insensitive matching.
sections.lower:
from ttsready import overridescope, speechoverride, textunit, prepare_units

unit = textunit("chapter-1", "acme ships 2 kg parcels.", "en-us")
company = speechoverride("acme", "a c m e")  # all units
weight = speechoverride(
    "kg",
    "kilograms",
    scope=overridescope("unit", "chapter-1"),
)
result = prepare_units((unit,), overrides=(company, weight))




the default match mode is word. use match="literal" to match a substring inside a larger token. the default is case-sensitive; set case_sensitive=false for case-insensitive matching.

sections.heading: Exact occurrence
sections.text:
For a correction that applies only to one occurrence, use source-relative half-open offsets:

from ttsready import OverrideScope, SpeechOverride, TextUnit, prepare_units

unit = TextUnit("caption-1", "Use ACME here, not ACME there.", "en-US")
first_start = unit.text.index("ACME")
override = SpeechOverride(
    "ACME",
    "A C M E",
    scope=OverrideScope(
        "occurrence",
        unit.id,
        first_start,
        first_start + len("ACME"),
    ),
)
result = prepare_units((unit,), overrides=(override,))




An occurrence override must exactly select its declared source surface. It cannot overlap a protected span.

sections.heading: Precedence and conflicts
sections.text:
More specific overrides take precedence: occurrence-scoped overrides, then unit-scoped overrides, then global overrides. A higher-priority overlapping rule wins and a lower-priority rule is reported in result.issues. Equally ranked overlapping overrides with different spoken text raise OverrideConflictError; resolve that conflict in caller policy before preparation.

Override IDs are deterministic when omitted. They identify the policy and scope; change IDs identify source occurrences independently of the selected replacement. Override provenance can carry JSON-safe caller metadata.

sections.heading: Ownership boundary
sections.text:
ttsready owns speech-preparation policy and source-relative results. It is an API-only transformation library, not an application pipeline.

Two APIs serve different callers: prepare_run() is the low-level primitive for compilers that already own linguistic and sentence analysis; prepare_text() and prepare_units() provide review-oriented preparation with overrides, context, QA, and aggregate results. They share one TTSReady-owned Spokenform adapter.

caller-owned source or speech pipeline
                │
       ┌────────┴────────┐
       ▼                 ▼
prepare_run(...)   prepare_text()/prepare_units()
compiler-facing    review-oriented
       │                 │
       ▼                 ▼
PreparedRun +      PreparedUnit / PreparationResult
SourceOutputMap

sections.text:
The supported Python API is the set exported from the root ttsready package via ttsready.__all__. It is source-neutral: callers provide text and explicit language values, and TTSReady does not accept paths or format-specific document objects.

The public preparation surface has three levels: prepare_run(), prepare_text(), and prepare_units().

sections.heading: Prepare a compiler-owned run
sections.text:
prepare_run() is the low-level source-neutral primitive for a compiler or pipeline that already owns linguistic and sentence analysis. It returns a PreparedRun with source/output text, changes, generic issues, language, and an exact SourceOutputMap. It does not apply SpeechOverride, build UnitContext, split sentences, or create aggregate fingerprints.

from ttsready import LinguisticToken, prepare_run

source = "Dr. Smith uses 2 kg."
run = prepare_run(
    source,
    language="en-US",
    linguistic_tokens=(LinguisticToken(0, 3, text="Dr.", pos="PROPN", tag="NNP"),),
    preserve_run_boundaries=True,
)

run.spoken_text
run.changes
run.source_map.map_source_span(0, 3)
run.source_map.to_dict()  # diagnostic representation; not result serialization

sections.heading: Protected spans and profiles
sections.text:
Protected spans are half-open offsets into the exact input string. They are not transformed, and an overlapping override is reported rather than applied:

from ttsready import ProtectedSpan, prepare_text

prepared = prepare_text(
    "Use SKU-42 now.",
    language="en-US",
    protected_spans=(ProtectedSpan(4, 10, reason="inventory identifier"),),
)




PreparationProfile contains conservative backend and normalization options. Its defaults avoid whitespace/Unicode normalization and preserve residual sequences; number, abbreviation, and structured-value expansion remain enabled. Pass a profile explicitly when reproducibility requires a particular policy.

sections.heading: Mapping and context
sections.text:
SpokenChange records a stable ID, unit ID, original and replacement text, source/output offsets, transformation stages, kind, and JSON-safe provenance. The offsets are half-open Python string indices. Apply a change set with apply_changes(source_text, changes); it verifies that every source span still selects the expected source text and rejects overlapping or stale changes.

SpokenChange.language is the effective language reported by the preparation backend for that individual replacement. TTSReady preserves it exactly, even when its spelling or case differs from PreparedRun.language or PreparedUnit.language; if the backend supplies no per-change language, the value is None. sections.heading: Text chunking
sections.text:
split_prepared_text(text, *, language, max_chars) -> tuple[TextChunk, ...] chunks the string supplied by the caller; it does not prepare, normalize, or otherwise transform it. Splits prefer sentence boundaries and fall back to smaller pieces as needed to satisfy the character limit.


Every TextChunk.text is an exact slice of the original string, and start/end are source-relative half-open offsets.


part is zero-based; chunks concatenate back to the exact input and each chunk has at most max_chars characters.


Empty input returns (). A max_chars value below 1 raises ValueError.

sections.heading: Residual QA
sections.text:
Preparation includes non-mutating residual checks and attaches findings to each PreparedUnit.issues and aggregate PreparationResult.issues. Findings identify a code, severity, unit, optional source span, text, message, and JSON-safe provenance.

Use check_units() to inspect caller text without preparing or rewriting it:

from ttsready import TextUnit, check_units

issues = check_units((TextUnit("caption-1", "Meet at 10:30.", "en-US"),))
for issue in issues:
    print(issue.code, issue.severity, issue.text, issue.message)

sections.heading: Quickstart
sections.text:
prepare_text() prepares one caller-owned string with an explicit language. It returns a PreparedUnit containing the original text, spoken text, exact changes, issues, and sentence context.

from ttsready import prepare_text

prepared = prepare_text("A 2 kg parcel.", language="en-US", unit_id="parcel")
print(prepared.spoken_text)

for change in prepared.changes:
    print(
        f"{change.source!r} -> {change.replacement!r} "
        f"(source {change.source_start}:{change.source_end}, "
        f"output {change.output_start}:{change.output_end})"
    )




Both spans are half-open Python string offsets. The source span selects the original occurrence; the output span selects its replacement in spoken_text.

sections.heading: Compiler-owned runs
sections.text:
If your pipeline already performs linguistic analysis and segmentation, use prepare_run() instead of wrapping the run in review-oriented TextUnit context:

from ttsready import LinguisticToken, prepare_run

source = "Dr. Smith measured 2 kg."
run = prepare_run(
    source,
    language="en-US",
    linguistic_tokens=(LinguisticToken(0, 3, text="Dr.", pos="PROPN"),),
    preserve_run_boundaries=True,
)
print(run.spoken_text)
output_start, output_end = run.source_map.map_source_span(0, 3)

sections.heading: Multiple units
sections.text:
Use TextUnit and prepare_units() for multiple text segments. Each unit supplies its own language and stable caller ID; order is preserved.

from ttsready import TextUnit, prepare_units

result = prepare_units(
    (
        TextUnit("chapter-1", "2 kg", "en-US", role="body"),
        TextUnit("caption-1", "Bonjour.", "fr-FR", role="caption"),
    )
)

for unit in result.units:
    print(unit.unit_id, unit.language, unit.spoken_text)
print(result.stats.units_processed)




The aggregate result also exposes combined changes, issues, statistics, and profile/override/runtime/output fingerprints. No file, format object, or document wrapper is needed. See overrides, residual QA, and reproducibility for the rest of the API.

sections.heading: Runtime versions
sections.text:
ttsready.__version__ is the package’s public runtime version. Builds derive it from Git tags with setuptools-scm, which generates ttsready/_version.py for installed distributions. A source checkout without generated version metadata reports 0+unknown; release artifacts must carry the exact tag-derived version, never this fallback. runtime_versions() returns the TTSReady, Spokenform, and Phrasplit versions used by the runtime fingerprint.

The runtime fingerprint covers ttsready, spokenform, and phrasplit. The prepared-output fingerprint covers ordered unit IDs and their spoken text. profile_fingerprint(), override_fingerprint(), runtime_fingerprint(), and unit_fingerprint() are available for caller-defined verification or record layouts. sections.heading: JSON round trips
sections.text:
Preparation results can be serialized to built-in JSON values and restored:

import json
from ttsready import TextUnit, prepare_units, result_from_dict, result_to_dict

result = prepare_units((TextUnit("unit-1", "2 kg", "en-US"),))
encoded = json.dumps(result_to_dict(result), sort_keys=True)
restored = result_from_dict(json.loads(encoded))
assert restored == result




New ttsready.preparation.v2 payloads include SpokenChange.language as a string or null. Older v2 payloads without that key deserialize with language=None. This additive metadata does not change existing fingerprints.
